architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added sqlx as a workspace dependency with PostgreSQL-specific features enabled
architecture_decisions.rationale: The sqlx crate provides async, compile-time checked SQL queries with PostgreSQL support. Adding it as a workspace dependency ensures consistent versioning across all packages. The specific features (postgres, derive, macros, uuid, chrono, ipnet, json) were selected to support the database operations needed for authentik while keeping the dependency tree minimal.
alternatives_considered: Using a different ORM like diesel

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Made the db module conditional on the 'core' feature flag in ak-common
architecture_decisions.rationale: This allows consumers of ak-common to opt into database functionality only when needed. The 'core' feature was chosen as the gate since database operations are fundamental to the core functionality of authentik. This prevents pulling in sqlx dependencies for packages that don't need database access.

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Implemented a singleton database pool with OnceLock for thread-safe initialization
architecture_decisions.rationale: Using OnceLock ensures the database pool is initialized exactly once and provides safe concurrent access. This pattern follows Rust's ownership model while providing global access to the connection pool. The pool is configured with connection limits (min 1, max 4) and health checks to maintain database reliability.
alternatives_considered: Passing pool instances through dependency injection
Creating new pools for each component

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Implemented dynamic reconfiguration of database connections when config changes
architecture_decisions.rationale: The database watcher task listens for config change events and updates connection options without restarting the application. This is critical for production environments where database credentials or SSL settings might need to be rotated. The solution uses the existing arbiter pattern for event-driven architecture.
alternatives_considered: Requiring application restart for config changes

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added comprehensive unit tests covering initialization, queries, config updates, and connection creation
architecture_decisions.rationale: Tests verify that the database utilities work correctly with the actual configuration system and can handle dynamic changes. The tests use the existing config initialization pattern and verify both pool and individual connection functionality. Each test sets up the proper environment by changing to the project root directory.

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Updated CI workflow to include runtime dependencies for database tests
architecture_decisions.rationale: The database tests require a running PostgreSQL instance, so the CI configuration needed to include 'runtime' dependencies alongside 'rust'. This ensures tests can actually connect to a database and verify the functionality works end-to-end.

tickets.title: Add sqlx dependency and database utilities module
tickets.description: Added sqlx as a workspace dependency and created a new db module in ak-common package with connection pooling, configuration management, and testing

implementation_summary:
The implementation creates a new database utilities module within the ak-common package that provides shared PostgreSQL functionality for the entire codebase. The core design centers around a singleton connection pool managed by OnceLock, ensuring thread-safe initialization and access. The module integrates deeply with the existing configuration system, supporting dynamic reconfiguration through an event-driven watcher that listens for config changes via the arbiter pattern.

Key architectural patterns include feature gating (the db module is only available when the 'core' feature is enabled), comprehensive error handling using eyre::Result, and integration with the existing authentik configuration structure for PostgreSQL settings. The implementation follows Rust best practices with proper ownership management, async/await patterns, and compile-time type checking through sqlx's macro system.

The solution is designed to be reusable across different services while maintaining the existing codebase patterns. It includes thorough unit tests that verify initialization, query execution, configuration updates, and individual connection creation. The CI pipeline was updated to ensure database tests can run with proper runtime dependencies, maintaining the project's testing rigor.
